references.text: This verse contains the original command to make the breastplate (חֹשֶׁן) with skilled workmanship, from gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen—exactly the same materials mentioned in Exodus 39:8.
Describes how the ephod was to be made with the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen. The breastplate was to be made in the same way as the ephod.
Describes the making of the ephod with the same materials as the breastplate: gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.
Mentions the craftsmen whom God filled with wisdom to perform skilled work (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב), the same expression used for the making of the breastplate.
The tent curtains of the tabernacle were also to be made of fine twisted linen, blue and purple wool, and scarlet yarn with skilled workmanship.
The making of the ephod in 39:2 confirms that the work was done exactly as commanded, parallel to the making of the breastplate.
